points.description: States that arrays are passed by reference (i.e., the function receives the array's address/reference to the original array, not a copy).
points.partial_credit: Award 1.5 if the student says the function works on/modifies the original array or passes the address but does not use the term 'by reference'.

points.description: Correctly distinguishes from pass by value: the array elements are not copied, so changes made inside the function affect the original array.
points.partial_credit: Award 1 if only says changes affect the original, without stating that no copy is made (or vice versa).

rubric.notes: Full marks require the precise statement that arrays are passed by reference, plus the contrast with pass by value (no copy made, original array modified). Saying 'by value' or that a copy is made earns nothing for either point. Vague answers that merely mention functions or pointers without saying reference/original array earn nothing.
